mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically each of the last three weeks (-9.1 to -6.9 to -5.1 to -3.4). This momentum reflects accumulating consumer confidence and habituation to reduced restrictions, which should continue to push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages lower than over the last 28 days despite the prior four-week monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility crosses above -25 percent from baseline for two consecutive weeks, it signals a critical mass of commuters and shoppers returning to public transport corridors that feed retail precincts, which should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -25 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -31.9 at t-3w to -27.7 at t-0w, approaching -25 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines within two weeks after TRANSIT sustains above -25 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility compounds: commuters returning to workplaces via transit generate incidental retail trips (lunch, errands, shopping on the way home), so joint upward movement in both series produces a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone would predict.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -8.0 to -6.7 and TRANSIT improved from -31.9 to -27.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no larger than what would be predicted from WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-to-late December in Sydney coincides with pre-Christmas holiday shopping and summer leisure activity, a seasonal demand surge that independently boosts RETAIL_REC regardless of marginal changes in other mobility categories, overriding any plateau in workplace or transit recovery.
candidate_trigger: decision date falls within 10 days of Christmas
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point is 2020-12-15, within the pre-Christmas shopping window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 2-4 weeks despite the pre-Christmas period, suggesting seasonal demand did not materialize or was offset by restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are spending less time at home and resuming out-of-home routines, a behavioral shift that mechanically translates into higher retail and recreation visits within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 4.0 at t-3w to 3.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (greater than 5 points) indicates outdoor recreation is being curtailed, possibly due to weather or local advisories, causing displaced recreational demand to substitute toward indoor retail and recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS drops more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -10.0 at t-1w to -16.4 at t-0w, a 6.4 point drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks following a PARKS drop exceeding 5 points, or RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction instead of substituting.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near a stable positive range (2.3 to 5.7) across all four weeks, indicating no new policy restrictions on essential services have been imposed; this policy stability signals continued freedom of movement that supports ongoing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained positive and stable, ranging 2.3 to 5.7 across the four weeks
regime_hint: steady state, no new restrictions announced
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable and positive, indicating the policy-stability proxy is unreliable.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply negative relative to baseline (TRANSIT around -28, WORKPLACES around -7), jointly indicating residual policy-driven restrictions on commuting and office occupancy that continue to cap retail footfall growth; their combined depressed state suppresses RETAIL_REC gains more than either alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -27.7 and WORKPLACES at -6.7 at t-0w remain far below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises strongly over the next week even while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply negative, indicating no joint suppression effect.
